title: Tenant time-zone aware quota epochs + reconciliation job for reserved capacity
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: Current quota resets in the billing system are anchored to a single global epoch (UTC and several rolling-window implementations). Customers who expect calendar-month or local-day boundaries (for example, customers in APAC who purchase reserved capacity aligned to local billing cycles) observe apparent over-usage or unexpected burst behaviour when their local month/day boundary does not match the platform epoch. This leads to disputed invoices, support tickets, and incorrect burst bucket refills for Reserved capacity tenants.
motivation: Reduce invoice disputes and improve predictable behaviour for reserved-capacity tenants who require local-calendar alignment. Provide clear, testable invariants for quota accounting across the platform so downstream billing, reporting and console displays remain consistent.
proposal_summary: Introduce a per-tenant quota epoch that can be anchored to a tenant time zone (tenant_tz) and a deterministic reconciliation job that keeps the global accounting consistent. Implement a dual-counter model (local_epoch_counter + global_granular_counter) to allow local resets without losing global auditability. Add a background reconciliation worker that detects drift, auto-applies corrective credit/debit entries, and emits compensating events for observability.
acceptance_criteria: New tenants can opt into time-zone anchored monthly/daily quota resets via tenant_tz metadata
Reserved capacity burst buckets refill at the tenant-local boundary for opted-in tenants
All corrective adjustments are recorded as idempotent journal entries and visible in billing audit logs
Reconciliation job has deterministic convergence (no more than 2 reconciliation passes for typical clock skew cases)
No billing/regression test failures across the existing suite and sandbox tenants before rollout
Console reflects tenant-local quota windows in UI and API responses for opted-in tenants
implementation_notes: DB: add tenant_quota_epoch (ISO date) and tenant_tz fields to tenants table; create tenant_quota_counters table with columns: tenant_key, epoch_start, local_counter, global_counter, last_reconciled_at
API: expose tenant_quota_policy config (enum: GLOBAL_UTC | LOCAL_TZ_MONTHLY | LOCAL_TZ_DAILY) in admin and onboarding APIs
Runtime: when serving requests, use a fast lookup cache (in-memory / Redis) for tenant epoch policy to avoid added latency on hot paths

Reconciliation: hourly worker that scans tenants with LOCAL_* policies; for each tenant compute expected local epoch, compare local_counter vs recorded usage and enqueue compensating journal entries if delta > threshold
Backfill: add a migration tool that computes starting local_epoch for existing tenants using historical token timestamps; run in dry-run then in windowed batches
Observability: add metrics: quota_epoch_shift_events, reconciliation_actions, reconciliation_latency_seconds, reconciled_tenants_count; add dashboard for cross-tenant reconciliation state
API compatibility: default behaviour for tenants without tenant_tz remains GLOBAL_UTC to avoid behavioural changes
Performance trade-offs: reconciliation scans must be parallelized by shard key and rate-limited to avoid DB contention; prefer idempotent upserts for counters
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Large backfill may place high load on DB and billing pipeline. Mitigation: windowed backfill with throttling; use read replicas and a dedicated backfill worker fleet
Risk: Clock skew between services could cause transient double-counting. Mitigation: use event timestamps normalized to UTC and reconcile with grace window and idempotent journal entries
Risk: Console UX confusion if tenants flip policy mid-cycle. Mitigation: disallow switching policy during an active local epoch or surface a warning and create transitional invoice adjustments
Risk: Late-arriving usage events. Mitigation: reconciliation job applies a configurable late-arrival grace period (default 2 hours) before finalizing epoch counters
migration_plan_summary: Phase 1: DB schema change behind feature flag (no behaviour change). Phase 2: backfill historical starting epochs for opted-in tenants in sandbox; run reconciliation dry-run in production for 48 hours and compare vs current invoices. Phase 3: enable LOCAL_* policy for subset of customers (canary 5%), monitor metrics. Phase 4: full rollout and deprecate legacy per-tenant hacks.
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch arithmetic (edge cases: DST transitions, leap seconds not relevant but test leap-day boundary)
Integration tests that simulate cross-timezone tenants with load patterns across month boundaries
Load test: reconciliation worker against synthetic dataset of 100k tenants with 1k req/s historical events to validate throughput
End-to-end billing smoke: create sandbox tenants, opt into LOCAL_TZ_MONTHLY, generate usage spanning boundary and assert final invoice adjustments match expectations
Chaos test: simulate reconciliation worker restart and verify idempotence of journal entries
Manual QA: product session to verify console displays and API responses for tenant-local windows
rollout_plan: Canary to 5% of reserved-capacity tenants (low-risk, active support plan flag). Monitor reconciliation_actions metric and billing-disputes Slack channel. If >0.5% of canary tenants show non-convergent reconciliations after 24h, rollback. Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% over 2 weeks with manual checkpoints.
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: sudden spike in compensating_journal_amounts (>10x baseline) -> P1
Dashboard: per-region reconciled progress, per-tenant drift histogram, recent corrective entries list
notes_and_links: Slack thread: #billing-ops April rollouts (link redacted for ticket)
